articles.title: Les Mis\'erables Dialogue: A film-based network representation of social communication
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.13148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we revisit the classic Les Mis\'erables benchmark network from the perspective of social communication. Using the 1998 film adaptation of the novel, we construct the publicly available Les Mis\'erables Dialogue temporal text network, which explicitly distinguishes speakers, addressees, and other recipients of each utterance, along with its content and timing. articles.title: Extracting Illicit-Rich Subgraph from Transaction Networks via Feed-Guided Shortest Paths
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.13280v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study investigative subgraph extraction for Anti-Money Laundering (AML) transaction graphs using the Shortest Paths Network Search Algorithm (SPNSA), which aggregates shortest paths among a small input feed of entities. Since SPNSA is highly sensitive to the feed choice, we evaluate several graph-only feed selection strategies and propose a motif-based coherent feed selection method. articles.title: A data-driven heuristic-ensemble method for behavioural inference in collective-risk dilemma experiments
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.13595v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The collective-risk dilemma has become a paradigm for studying cooperation in a wide variety of social experiments, initiatives that generate increasingly rich datasets describing individual actions over successive decision-making processes. Beyond the purely descriptive analysis of such empirical datasets, a methodological framework is required to interpret and reproduce the observed dynamics, a scheme that may be skewed by exogenous biases. articles.title: Studying Comics at Scale with Artificial Intelligence: The PAGE Framework and Three Studies of American Comics and Japanese Manga
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.13840v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Comics are one of the great visual records of the twentieth century: hundreds of thousands of pages in which a mass readership saw its leaders, its wars and its heroes. Most of this record has never been studied as a whole; comics scholarship proceeds one book at a time. We argue that artificial intelligence, including generative models, can change this to the benefit of the medium itself. articles.title: Complementarity, Augmentation, or Substitutivity? The Impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on the U.S. Federal Workforce
articles.summary: arXiv:2503.09637v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This study applies a multi-stage Retrieval-Augmented Generation system, which grounds large language model assessments in curated evidence, to evaluate generative AI's near-term impact on knowledge, skills, and abilities across several hundred federal occupational series. articles.title: ABLEIST: Intersectional Disability Bias in LLM-Generated Hiring Scenarios
articles.summary: arXiv:2510.10998v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly under scrutiny for perpetuating identity-based discrimination in high-stakes domains such as hiring, particularly against people with disabilities (PwD). However, existing research remains largely Western-centric, overlooking how intersecting forms of marginalization--such as gender and caste--shape experiences of PwD in the Global South. articles.title: Indirect Geoeconomic Influence: A Switching Dynamical Systems Framework for Mechanism Design
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.07940v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a formal framework for analyzing indirect geoeconomic influence. The influencing state (sender) does not attempt to change a target nation's policy directly. Instead, the sender restructures the target's internal political economy so that its own citizens, firms, and institutions generate the compliance pressure.
